Subject: FintechCo — logging & redaction controls follow-up

Hi Sasha / security team,

Thanks again for the time today — great to hear more about FintechCo's production needs. Per our call, I wanted to recap the logging & redaction items and propose next steps so we can validate a configuration that meets your compliance and incident-investigation needs.

High-level ask summary from the call:
- Types of data to treat as sensitive: account numbers (PAN/IBAN), SSNs, email addresses, phone numbers, internal user IDs.
- Logs of interest: request + response bodies, request/response headers, tracing IDs/trace context.
- Retention targets: prefer 90 days for raw request logs, 7 years for audit-level events (we talked about roll-up retention).
- Residency: primary requirement is US-only storage for logs; EU option if you need EU residency for specific environments.

What Redwood can provide (initial options):
- Logging disabled by default on hosted API. We can enable request/response logging with configurable redaction profiles at ingestion.
- Redaction levels: "partial" (mask emails, PANs, SSNs, phone numbers), "strict" (mask most free-text fields, keep only structured metadata), or "none" (no redaction).
- Header handling: option to strip headers, mask header values (e.g., Authorization), or pseudonymize trace IDs (e.g., hash before storage).
- Traceability: we can maintain hashed trace IDs so you can correlate events without storing raw trace values.
- Retention controls: per-environment retention windows and separate audit logs with longer retention.

I've attached a short doc (redaction_controls_v1.pdf) and a sample log-snippet showing how masking would be applied (sample_log_snippet.txt).

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the priority sensitive fields (PAN/SSN/email/etc) and whether you need raw trace IDs preserved or hashed?
2) If you can share a short list of sample log lines (PII redacted on your side), we can produce a sample obfuscation pseudocode and a sanitized example for sign-off.
3) Propose a 30-min follow-up next week with your security engineer + our SRE (Dev) to walk the redaction rules and retention windows.

Happy to iterate.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments — helpful. A few clarifications from our security team after reviewing the doc: 

1) Sensitive fields we need to ensure are redacted at ingestion: full PANs, SSNs, bank account numbers/IBAN, full email addresses (we accept hashed/email local-part masking), phone numbers, and any customer-identified numbers (customer IDs).
2) Headers: we need Authorization removed from any stored logs. Trace IDs — we prefer they be pseudonymized (hashed) so we can correlate across services but the raw values cannot be stored in plain text.
3) Request/response bodies: we cannot allow full plaintext storage of prompts/LLM responses for production traffic. We need an option where the full text is never stored — only token-level metrics and redacted/structured extracts.
4) Retention: 90 days for searchable raw logs is acceptable; audit roll-ups must be retained for 7 years. Is that supported in Hosted? Also need confirmation that EU residency is available for EU regions.

Action items for Redwood: can you provide:
- Sample pseudocode for the redaction rules (regex + field-level config)
- Example of what a masked request/response looks like for an LLM prompt containing names, PANs, and emails
- SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent artifacts — we can sign an NDA if required.

We'd like to schedule the follow-up meeting next Tue or Wed (your timezone). I'll loop in our infra lead if needed.

Regards,

Hi Sasha — thanks for the detailed notes, this is exactly the kind of input we want before we lock config. Quick responses inline:

1) Sensitive fields: we will support redaction for PANs, SSNs, IBANs, emails, phone numbers, and common identifier patterns. Redaction is rule-driven (regex + field name mapping) and can be extended for custom fields.

2) Headers: Authorization and similar secrets are removed by default from stored headers when logging is enabled. For trace IDs we offer two options: a) strip entirely, or b) store a one-way hash (SHA256) of the trace id so you can correlate without raw values. We can enable hashed-trace-ids for your environment.

3) Request/response text: Hosted API can be configured so that full prompts/responses are NOT stored in plaintext. Options:
   - No-text mode: request/response bodies are not stored at all (only metadata and derived signals).
   - Redacted-text mode: free text is run through redaction rules and a sanitized copy is stored.

4) Retention/residency: Hosted supports environment-level retention windows (e.g., 90 days). Audit roll-ups can be exported to an S3 bucket with configurable lifecycle; we can support 7-year retention for exported audit artifacts. EU residency: yes — we have EU regions where logs remain in-region. We'll document region mapping for your legal team.

Attachments and examples: the attached sample_log_snippet.txt includes a couple of masked examples (email->"e***@example.com", PAN->"**** **** **** 1234"). I'm including a short pseudocode snippet below for quick review. We'll produce a cleaned deliverable for your infra team before the meeting.

Pseudocode (high-level):
- for each incoming request:
  - parse structured fields and run configured regex list against free-text fields
  - if pattern match -> replace with mask token (e.g., "[REDACTED_EMAIL]") or keep last 4 digits for PANs
  - for headers -> if header in blocklist -> remove; if header in hashlist -> hash(value)
  - if environment flag NO_TEXT = true -> discard request/response bodies after metrics extraction

Next steps:
- I'll have Dev (SRE) prepare a sanitized sample showing strict vs partial redaction in JSON-lines format and share before our call.
- Proposed meeting: Tue Jul 14, 2026 10:00-10:30 PT — does that work for you + infra lead?
- I'll also attach SOC 2 summary and redaction_controls_v1.pdf to the meeting invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
